head-on.title: Head-on
head-on.brief: Two airliners fly towards each other at the same level. Spot it early and separate them.
head-on.goal: Keep at least 5 NM or 1000 ft between TRN101 and TRN202, acting well before the alert.

crossing.title: Crossing at right angles
crossing.brief: Two aircraft cross at 90° at the same level. Their paths meet over the middle of the sector.
crossing.goal: Separate TRN303 and TRN404 with one clearance.

climb-through.title: Climbing through traffic
climb-through.brief: A departure climbs into your sector towards FL340 while traffic crosses at FL300.
climb-through.goal: Keep TRN505's climb clear of TRN606; the smallest change is often to stop the climb.

overtaking.title: Catching up
overtaking.brief: A fast jet follows a slower one on the same track and level. The gap is closing.
overtaking.goal: Keep TRN707 at least 5 NM behind TRN808 or 1000 ft away from it.

blocked-request.title: A request you can't grant yet
blocked-request.brief: TRN909 asks to climb to FL340, but traffic is about to cross its path at FL320.
blocked-request.goal: Keep everyone separated and give TRN909 its level as soon as it is safe.

double-trouble.title: The obvious level is taken
double-trouble.brief: A head-on pair at FL310, with traffic at FL320 right beside them; a second conflict follows.
double-trouble.goal: Resolve both conflicts without creating a new one: check the level is free first.

welcome.title: Welcome to your practice sector
welcome.body:
As an air traffic controller your job is to keep every aircraft in your sector safely separated (at least 5 NM horizontally or 1000 ft vertically) while getting them where they want to go efficiently.

This tutorial runs in a private training sector: the traffic is scripted and nothing you do affects other controllers. It takes about 10–15 minutes. You can leave at any time and resume later.

scope.title: Find your way around the scope
scope.body: The scope is a 3D map of Europe. Aircraft carry a data block (label) with their details.
scope.goal: Zoom in on the Alps region (around Marseille, Geneva and Turin) so the training traffic fills your screen.
scope.how:
• Pan: drag with the left mouse button (one finger on touch screens).
  • Zoom: mouse wheel (pinch on touch screens).
  • Rotate / tilt: drag with the right mouse button (two fingers on touch screens).

sector.title: Take your sector
sector.body:
Airspace is divided into sectors. Each region is also split vertically into layers: Lower (up to FL245), Upper (FL245–345) and High (above FL345). A controller is responsible for every aircraft inside the sectors they hold; nobody else can clear them.

You can see everyone's sectorization: each controller has a colour, the AI is violet, free sectors are faint outlines.
sector.how: Open {list} (or press My sectors {bar}), find Alps and press Take on the U layer.

datablock.title: Read a data block
datablock.body:
Each data block shows, line by line:

  • Callsign (e.g. TRN303), plus H for heavy aircraft.
  • Flight level (290 = 29,000 ft), a trend arrow ↑/↓ when climbing or descending, then the cleared level.
  • Ground speed in knots and any lateral instruction (heading or direct-to).

The line ahead of each aircraft is its speed vector: where it will be in 2 minutes.
datablock.how: Click (tap) the aircraft or its data block. Its flight strip opens with all its details and the clearance controls.

heading.title: Give a heading
heading.body: Clearances are instructions to a pilot. You can type them on the command line using ATC shorthand. The pilot reads the clearance back on the radio and executes it after a few seconds.
heading.how:
Click the command line (or press /) and type TRN303 TR 20D, then Enter. With TRN303 selected you can omit the callsign: TR 20D.

Other forms: TL 270 turn left heading 270 · H 090 fly heading 090.

direct.title: Proceed direct to a fix
direct.body: Instead of vectoring, you can send an aircraft straight to a navaid or airport. After passing it, the aircraft rejoins its route.
direct.goal: Clear TRN303 direct to a nearby navaid.
direct.how: In TRN303's flight strip, pick a fix from the Direct list and press DCT. Or type TRN303 DCT followed by the fix identifier.

resume.title: Resume own navigation
resume.body: When you no longer need an aircraft off its route, let the crew continue on their own.
resume.goal: Tell TRN303 to resume own navigation.
resume.how: Press Resume own nav in the flight strip, or type TRN303 RON.

level.title: Change level
level.body: Vertical clearances are the most common tool: climbing or descending an aircraft by 1000 ft is often enough to keep it clear of others.
level.how: In the flight strip set Level to 330 (use + / −) and press Climb. Or type TRN303 C 330. It stays inside your sector: Alps Upper goes up to FL345.

spot.title: Spot a conflict
spot.body:
Two new aircraft, TRN101 and TRN202, are flying towards each other at the same level. The short-term conflict alert (STCA) predicts losses of separation up to 2 minutes ahead: the aircraft turn amber and the alert appears in the Alerts list.

Good controllers see it coming before the alert: the coach gives credit for acting early.
spot.goal: Wait for the STCA between TRN101 and TRN202, then select one of them.
spot.how: Open {list} and click the alert. It appears in about 2 minutes. To wait less, set 2× or 4× speed{speed}.

resolve.title: Resolve the conflict
resolve.body: Separate them before they get closer than 5 NM at the same level. A vertical solution is usually the simplest: move one of them 1000 ft up or down.
resolve.goal: Give TRN101 or TRN202 a new level and keep them separated until they have passed.
resolve.how: Select one and type e.g. TRN101 C 320 or TRN202 D 300. Not sure? End the command with ? to see its predicted future in 3D before you send it, or press H for a hint from the coach. The goal is reached once they have passed each other without a loss of separation.
resolve.failed: Separation was lost. Press Replay situation to try again: act as soon as the STCA appears.

coach.title: Meet your coach
coach.body:
An AI coach follows every situation in your sectors and grades your decision (A to E): safety, timing and efficiency, compared with the AI's own answer. Choose how much it helps:

  • Evaluate: grades only, as in an exam.
  • Hints: ask for a hint (H): where to look, what is wrong, a solution.
  • Advise: every option with its predicted outcome and why, plus the AI's advice.
  • Demonstrate: the AI resolves your situations and explains each move.
coach.how: Set Coach to Advise {bar}. The Decisions list then shows every option with its explanation; hover one to see its future in 3D.

request.title: Answer a pilot request
request.body: Pilots ask for what they need. TRN303 is at FL330, but its flight plan is at FL290, so the crew will soon request a descent. Unanswered requests expire and cost points.
request.goal: Grant TRN303’s request to descend to FL290.
request.how: When “TRN303, request descent FL290” appears on the radio, open {list} and press Issue on the approve option (or Accept the AI's advice). You can also type TRN303 D 290. Speed up time if you are waiting.

score.title: Time, grades and score
score.body:
After each situation the coach shows a grade (A–E) with a short explanation, and the Debrief brings them all together. The points score rewards safe, efficient work: +2 per aircraft handled, +10 per request granted, −2 per STCA, −10 per ignored request and −50 per loss of separation.

Live traffic always runs in real time. In training and in Replay scenarios you can speed up to 16×.
score.goal: Speed up the simulation to 2× or more.

ready.title: You are ready
ready.body:
Well done: you have navigated the scope, issued headings, direct-tos and level changes, resolved a conflict, met your coach and answered a pilot request.

Next: the Training center (🎓) has short exercises, each training one kind of decision, with a debrief after each. Or take a sector with live traffic. The tutorial stays available there too.

tutOffer.title: New here? Take the guided tutorial
tutOffer.p1: In about 10–15 minutes you will learn to read the scope, give clearances, resolve a conflict and answer pilot requests, step by step in a private practice sector. Nothing you do there affects other controllers.
tutOffer.p2: Strongly recommended before working live traffic. It is optional and always available in the Training center.
tutOffer.resume: You started it earlier: pick up where you left off.

coach.why.monitor_ok: No action needed: they pass {h} NM apart.
coach.why.monitor_ok_v: No action needed: they stay vertically separated.
coach.why.monitor_bad: Doing nothing loses separation in {t} s.
coach.why.best_h: Resolves it with the smallest change: {h} NM at the closest point.
coach.why.best_v: Resolves it with the smallest change: 1000 ft or more vertically.
coach.why.least_bad: Nothing keeps full separation; this shortens the loss to {d} s.
coach.why.costlier: Also safe, but a bigger change than {best}.
coach.why.tighter: Safe, but tighter: {h} NM at the closest point.
coach.why.equal_h: Just as good: an equally small change, {h} NM at the closest point.
coach.why.equal_v: Just as good: an equally small change, 1000 ft or more vertically.
coach.why.unsafe: Still loses separation, in {t} s ({d} s below the minima).
coach.why.approve_ok: Granting it is safe for the next 4 minutes.
coach.why.approve_bad: Granting it now loses separation with {other} in {t} s.
coach.why.intermediate_ok: The full request conflicts; this level is safe for now.
coach.why.intermediate: A partial step: safe, but the pilot still wants more.
coach.why.deny_ok: Keeps separation; grant it later, once {other} is clear.
coach.why.deny_worse: Safe, but the request can be granted: the pilot keeps waiting.
coach.fb.los: Separation was lost ({h} NM, {v} ft). Act as soon as the conflict shows: you had {lead} s.
coach.fb.no_action_los: No clearance was given and separation was lost. {best} would have kept them apart.
coach.fb.late: Resolved, but late: only {lead} s before the predicted loss. Aim for 90 s or more.
coach.fb.tight: Separated, but only just: {h} NM and {v} ft at the closest point. Act earlier for a clear margin.
coach.fb.costly: Safe, but a bigger change than needed: {best} would have done it.
coach.fb.extra: Safe, but you used {n} clearances where one was enough.
coach.fb.unneeded: No action was needed: they would have passed {h} NM apart.
coach.fb.good_h: Well done: resolved {lead} s ahead, {h} NM at the closest point.
coach.fb.good_v: Well done: resolved {lead} s ahead with vertical separation.
coach.fb.monitor_good: Right call: no action was needed and they passed safely.
coach.fb.req_slow: Granted safely, but the pilot waited {rt} s. Answer within a minute.
coach.fb.req_denied_ok: Good judgement: granting it would have caused a conflict.
coach.fb.req_denied_bad: It could have been granted safely; the pilot keeps waiting.
coach.fb.req_partial: A safe partial step, but the full request could have been granted.
coach.fb.req_unsafe: Your answer led to a conflict with {other}. Check the level is free first.
coach.fb.demo: Demonstration by the AI: not graded.
coach.hint.c2: {a} (FL{fa}) and {b} (FL{fb}) will be {h} NM apart in {t} s: under the {min} NM minimum with less than 1000 ft between them.
coach.hint.c2_clear: {a} and {b} are predicted to stay separated: {h} NM at the closest point.
coach.hint.r1_level: {a} is waiting for an answer: it wants FL{fl}.
coach.hint.r1_route: {a} is waiting for an answer: it wants to resume its own navigation.
coach.hint.r2_ok: It is free: granting it keeps separation.
coach.hint.r2_bad: It is not free: {other} is in the way.
coach.db.empty: No decisions were graded in this session.
coach.db.los: Separation was lost {n} time(s): that is the first thing to fix.
coach.db.hints: Hints used: {n}. Try the next attempt with fewer.
coach.db.next_pass: Next: the next drill, or this one at a stricter coach level.
coach.db.next_retry: Next: rewind to the situation you want to improve and try it again.
